column2: How do I open my website on another computer, with MAMP, WAMP or XAMPP?
column3: In “🌐 My website”: “⤓ Export ▾” → “📦 The whole site as .zip” (site-name-YYYY-MM-DD.zip). Unzip it wherever you like: a double-click on index.html is enough (pages, photos, scripts and the interactive map work without a server; the map background and Google fonts come from the Internet). With MAMP (Mac): copy the folder into htdocs, then http://localhost:8888/mon-site/. With WAMP: into www; with XAMPP: into htdocs, then http://localhost/mon-site/. Addresses are relative: it also works in a subfolder and with any web host. No need for PHP or a database. Everything is explained in LISEZ-MOI.html, in the .zip. As when publishing, no living person and no confidential record.

column2: How do I change the style of all elements of the same kind on my website?
column3: Choose an element in the preview: at the top of the right panel, “Apply to” offers “All .class elements” (the default when the element has a class) or “This element only”. With the class, your settings (colour, margins, size, alignment…) write a real rule in the site’s CSS, updated without duplicates: you see it change in the CSS tab, and what you type in the CSS comes back into the panel. “On hover” writes a :hover rule; “💻 Tablet” or “📱 Phone” writes the rule in an @media (and the preview switches to that size). ↶ ↷ undo and redo.

column2: Does the interactive map of my site move in the editor?
column3: Yes: in “🌐 My website”, a 🗺 map with “Interactive map” ticked can be moved (drag) and zoomed (＋ −, mouse wheel) directly in the preview, with the same small script and the same backgrounds as the exported site. A single click still selects it so you can set it up on the right.

column2: How do I get a real map background on my website?
column3: Choose the 🗺 Map block, then on the right “Map background”: the same list as Settings → Maps and base maps (Cassini, État-major, OpenStreetMap, satellite…). The map is made as an image with the credit of the background. “Interactive map”: in the published site, people can move it and zoom; it uses your background if allowed (OpenStreetMap, CARTO, OpenTopoMap, OpenHistoricalMap), otherwise the OpenStreetMap background; the image remains for anyone without JavaScript.

column2: How do I put my website online directly (Netlify, GitHub Pages, FTP)?
column3: In “🌐 My website”: “📤 Publish”. Netlify: create a free account, then a token (User settings → Applications → Personal access tokens) and paste it. GitHub Pages: a “fine-grained” token with Contents and Pages permissions; the repository is created if it does not exist. Secure FTP: the server, username and password given by your web host; the connection is always encrypted. The token or password stays on this computer: it is never shown or backed up with the database; “× Forget” erases it.

column2: Can I put the calculator on the desktop?
column3: Yes: 🪟 in the calculator’s bar, or Dashboard → “🪟 Desktop widgets…” → 🧮 Calculator. In the desktop app, it is a small separate window (always on top if you tick it); in a browser, a standalone .html file.

column2: How do I put a widget on my computer’s desktop (PC, Mac, Linux)?
column3: In the LCNDA desktop app: Dashboard → 🪟 on a widget (Today’s anniversaries, This week, Random person, Random image), or “🪟 Desktop widgets…” at the bottom of the column: On this day, An ancestor, Photo of the day, Countdown. A small frameless window, read-only; drag it by its title (it remembers its place); “Always on top” and “Start with the computer” are ticked in the same window; right-click on the widget: open LCNDA, remove it. In a browser, “⤓ Download the widget (.html)” gives a standalone file to keep in a tab (without living people).

column2: How do I write a letter, a story or a report in the app (the word processor)?
column3: Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → “📝 Word processor”, then “＋ New document” or “📋 Start from a template” (letter to the archives, request for a record, an ancestor’s story, visit report, research report, letter to the family, record transcription…). The text is written on real pages, with their margins: a paragraph that no longer fits moves to the next page. 💾 Save (⌘S) puts it in the list; “⚙️ Settings…” lets you save it on its own every few minutes.

column2: Do my documents work well in Word, LibreOffice or pandoc?
column3: Yes: ⤓ Export → Word (.docx), LibreOffice (.odt), RTF, Markdown, text or web page. Headings, bold, italic, colours, multi-level lists (the numbered list properly restarts at 1), tables with merged cells, images, notes, header and footer, landscape sections, comments and tracked changes are kept; RTF now writes real lists and vertical merges, and its accents are readable everywhere. ⤒ Import also reads files from Word, LibreOffice, Google Docs and pandoc (styles “Titre 1” or “Heading 1”, “List Bullet 2”, header of a previous section, YAML header of a Markdown file). ❓ Help (View menu) shows the answer over the document.

column2: How do I format text (styles, bold, lists, line spacing…)?
column3: Choose a style on the left of the bar (Normal, Heading 1 to 6, Quote, Caption…): headings form the outline, the table of contents and the 🧭 panel. Bold ⌘B, italic ⌘I, underline ⌘U, strikethrough, superscript, subscript, small caps, font (the single font list), size, colour and highlight. Bulleted and numbered lists: Tab goes down a level, Shift+Tab goes back up, Enter on an empty line leaves the list. The right panel (🎨) sets alignment, line spacing, space before and after, indents, drop cap, border and shading.

column2: How do I create my own styles, change style set or take those of a book?
column3: Right panel → Styles: “＋ New style” starts from the paragraph at the cursor; “✎ Edit the style” changes all paragraphs of that style at once. “Style set” (Classic, Modern, Elegant, Archives, Very readable, Old book) changes the fonts and colours of headings and text. Format → “📐 Take the styles of a book…” copies the styles of a book from the layout.

column2: How do I add an image, a table, a note or a link?
column3: Insert menu (or the bar): 🖼 Image (the single image window; a pasted or dropped image also goes into the media), ▦ Table (rows, columns, repeated header row) or 🧾 Table from the Spreadsheet, 🔗 Link (⌘K), ¹ Footnote (⌥⌘F, it shows at the bottom of its page) or endnote. Click an image to resize it by a corner; right-click: inline, square (text around it), top and bottom, caption. Table menu: rows and columns, merge (drag from one cell to another), sort, borders, shading.

column2: How do I cite a person, a place or a source from my database in a text?
column3: Insert → 👤 A person from the database (⇧⌘P): the usual picker, then what to write — the name (link to the record), the name and years, the birth or death with date and place. These texts follow the record: they are updated when the document is opened. 📍 A place, 🎞 A media item, 📖 a person’s biography (written by the app), 🌳 a small tree of 3 generations, 📊 a diagram. ❝ Cited source: the ready-made citation (4 styles), as a note; 📚 Bibliography picks it up on its own.

column2: How do I make a table of contents, an index or a bibliography?
column3: Insert → 📑 Table of contents (based on Heading 1, 2, 3, with page numbers), 🔤 Index (the people, places and words marked with “Mark for the index”) or 📚 Bibliography (the cited sources). They redo themselves when the text changes; a click on a line of the table of contents takes you there.

column2: How do I set up the page: size, margins, orientation, header and footer, watermark?
column3: Right panel → Page (or File → “📄 Size, margins and orientation…”): the app’s common sizes or “Custom size”, portrait or landscape, margins, page colour, watermark (DRAFT, COPY…). Double-click at the top or bottom of a page: the header and footer (page number, number of pages, title, date; different first page). Insert → “Section break”: what follows on a landscape page, for example for a large table; “▥ Columns” splits paragraphs into columns.

column2: How do several people review a text: tracked changes and comments?
column3: Tools → “✍ Track changes” (⌥⌘T): what is added is written in green underlined, what is deleted stays struck through in red, with the person’s name (Settings → “My name”). The ✍ panel lists the changes: ✓ Accept, ✗ Reject, or all at once. “Show changes”: all, simple or none. To comment: choose a passage then 💬 (⌥⌘M); you can reply, mark “Resolved”, delete (↶ Undo right after). Word and LibreOffice pick up the changes and the comments.

column2: How do I find and replace a word in a document?
column3: ⌘F (or 🔍): the search bar, with “Aa” (match case), “Whole word” and “Simple patterns” (* = some letters, ? = one letter, # = one digit). Each match is highlighted and listed in the 🧭 “Results” panel. ⇧⌘H goes straight to replacing: “Replace” or “Replace all” (↶ Undo right after).

column2: How do I open or save a Word (.docx) or LibreOffice (.odt) file?
column3: Open: “⤒ Import…” in the list (or File → Import, ⌘O): Word (.docx), LibreOffice (.odt), RTF, Markdown, text or web page; the window says what will come in before importing. Save: “⤓ Export ▾” at the top: Word, LibreOffice, PDF, RTF, Markdown, text, web page, or the tool’s own file; “Also store a copy in the media” keeps the .docx with the other documents. Everything is done in the app, with no extra software; a booby-trapped file (too big, zip bomb, XML with declarations, scripts) is refused or cleaned.

column2: How do I print or make a PDF of a document?
column3: “⤓ Export ▾” → 📄 PDF or 🖨 Print (⌘P): each page comes out exactly as on screen, with the header, footer, footnotes and watermark. For the PDF, choose “Save as PDF” as the printer.

column2: How do I keep versions of a document and compare them?
column3: File → “🕘 Save as new version” keeps the text as it is. File → “🕘 Versions…” opens the versions window: click a version to see it on the right, tick two versions (or “Now”) to compare them (removed words struck through in red, added ones in green), “↺ Go back to this version” (the current text is kept first, ↶ Undo possible).
